title: Keep your phone selected
summary: Remember a measured device in this browser and return directly to its benchmarks. Compare published translation timings on the iPhone 16 Pro Max and other named phones.

title: Find benchmarks for your hardware
summary: See which device details your browser reports, start with a measured reference, and find hardware by workload. Shared tests show comparable speeds side by side with the settings and source behind each result.

title: Compare two devices across nine workloads
summary: See published speeds and memory side by side. Choose a device tested under the same conditions in one click, or select a result to inspect its model, settings and source. Where a pair has no published result, the chart shows a measured example from another device.

title: Find local benchmarks by task or device
summary: Start with model quality, search evaluations by name or browse by workload. Model rows distinguish publishers and variants, and a compact device picker leads to matching performance measurements.

title: Explore local AI results by device and task
summary: Choose hardware to inspect published speed and memory results. Change evaluations within a workload, compare a model with a baseline, or share a link to the exact benchmark.

title: Find model weights and compare music and video models
summary: Browse published music, video and reranking results, compare device timings, and search the public Hugging Face catalog by task and format.

title: Compare local models by workload
summary: Explore published quality scores for language, embedding, image generation, transcription, speech synthesis and vision models. Each chart links to the evaluation behind its scores.

title: Local AI benchmarks
summary: Compare how quickly local models read prompts and generate text on the same Mac. Each result includes the model file, disk size, test settings and downloadable measurements.

title: Search benchmarks by name or workload
summary: Open the benchmark picker to read what each test measures. Search by name or by topics like pull requests and visual reasoning. The picker handles typos and supports keyboard navigation.

title: Argo-Bench opens the explorer
summary: Compare 60 reasoning settings across 16 Anthropic, OpenAI and Google models on 210 enterprise tasks. Plot Argo-Bench scores against model API cost or output tokens per task. The benchmark picker also adds Roboflow Visual Reasoning and IronBee Code Review.

title: Reasoning-effort curves and a benchmark picker
summary: The explorer opens on GameBench 2, with one point per tested effort setting and a curve for each model. Switch benchmarks to see Terminal-Bench agent runs or Epoch AI’s MirrorCode, GPQA Diamond and FrontierMath scores. GameBench 2 settings and costs are available in the release API, linked from the footer. The header has more room for navigation.

title: Documentation for the free API
summary: A new API page documents the free JSON endpoint behind every chart: each field, examples in the shell and JavaScript, how often the data changes, and each source’s license and the credit to keep with it. The endpoint needs no key, and any website may call it.

title: Scores from the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard
summary: Each model is now one point on the chart: its run on the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard, in the coding agent it was submitted with, against what that run cost per task or the output tokens it used. Model pages add Epoch AI’s MirrorCode, GPQA Diamond and FrontierMath scores and API prices from LiteLLM, and the release data lists each source’s license. Effort curves and the effort pages are gone, since no open source measures every setting; their addresses open Models.

title: Models grouped by lineup
summary: The explorer now opens on a lineup: current and superseded models, each grouped by tier so each lab’s models at the same level sit together, such as Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol. The lineup compares each model with today’s models. Releases still lists every model by date, against the models out on its release day.

title: Charts keep their axes when you switch models
summary: Every chart now draws on one scale for all models, so points stay in place when you pick another model, change the order or the comparison, or filter by lab. Before, the explorer fitted its axes to each model’s release-day field, so Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.2 Sol drew on different scales. Model, comparison and coding agent pages share the scale too.

title: Compare Codex, Claude Code and Antigravity CLI
summary: New pages put each lab’s coding agent side by side with every model and effort setting measured inside it: Coding Agent Index, cost per task, the three benchmarks behind the index and the official Terminal-Bench leaderboard. They also show how the same model scores alone and inside its agent.

title: Frontier stars follow At release and Live
summary: Stars in the release feed now follow the At release and Live switch and the lab filter, so a model’s row shows the same stars as its effort table. At release measures each model against the models out on its launch day. Model pages now list both: today’s stars and the stars a model earned on its release day.

title: Read a page for every model, matchup and effort step
summary: Each model now has its own page with scores and cost per task at every effort setting. Every two models that were current together get a head-to-head comparison, and each step up in effort, such as XHigh vs High, gets a page measured across models.

title: Count a model’s frontier settings in stars
summary: The Frontier badge is now a row of stars, one for each effort setting on the live cost frontier, so a model that leads at three budgets shows three stars.

title: Read effort curves in one table with distinct lab colors
summary: Inspect score, cost per task, and output tokens across every effort setting in a single table, with orange, blue, and green lab curves and live-frontier qualification.

title: Choose cookieless visits for the guide
summary: The blog’s privacy control lets you stop the guide from remembering visits on this browser.

title: A guide to reading the frontier
summary: Try a real cost-versus-score comparison inside Introducing aicharts, then open the explorer to compare releases for yourself.

title: Compare the effort settings behind a coding score
summary: Plot benchmark scores against dollars or output tokens per task. Compare a release with the models available on its launch day, or switch to the live field.

title: Take the release data with you
summary: The public JSON feed includes the source links, release dates, and effort-level measurements used in the explorer.
